queue.li_title: DSCR Cash-Out Refinance Seasoning: 3, 6, and 12 Months
queue.li_desc: Why seasoning windows exist, what they cost investors, and how the 3-month rule changes BRRRR math.
queue.li:
The number that decides how fast a BRRRR investor scales isn't the rehab budget or the ARV. It's the seasoning window.

Most DSCR lenders require 6-12 months of ownership before a cash-out refinance can use the new appraised value. That's 6-12 months of your capital parked in a finished, rented property doing nothing.

Our window is 3 months. No lease required at closing — the market-rent appraisal qualifies.

On a $110K cash-in deal, getting your capital back at month 3 instead of month 6 is the difference between four cycles a year and two. At portfolio scale, that compounds into an entirely different growth curve.

Hard money buys the project: 6-24 months, interest-only, sized off after-repair value, funds the rehab, closes in as little as 72 hours.

DSCR holds the property: 30-year term from 5.95%, qualified on the rent it produces — no tax returns, no DTI.

queue.li_title: DSCR Loans for Airbnb & Short-Term Rentals: How Financing Actually Works
queue.li_desc: How lenders qualify STR income, why market rent is the conservative anchor, and the STR-specific traps to avoid.
queue.li:
Short-term rentals can out-earn long-term rents two-to-one in the right market. Try explaining that to a bank.

Conventional lenders qualify you, not the property. They ignore projected nightly revenue and cap how many financed doors you can hold. So STR investors end up on DSCR loans, where the property qualifies itself.

The real question in short-term rental underwriting is which income number goes in the numerator. Some lenders will underwrite documented nightly-rate history, then charge for it with rate premiums, larger reserve requirements, and a haircut of 20% or more on the revenue — because nightly income is seasonal, volatile, and one city-council vote away from a licensing problem.

We use the conservative anchor instead: the appraiser's long-term market rent. If the property covers its payment as a plain 12-month rental, it qualifies. No lease required, no host history required, and every dollar you earn above market rent stays yours rather than becoming leverage priced against you.

A property that only works at 78% occupancy and peak nightly rates doesn't fail our underwriting. It fails risk management, and we would rather say so before you own it.

DSCR rates start at 5.95% on a 30-year fixed, and you close in your LLC.

The full breakdown: https://slacapital.ai/blog/dscr-loans-for-airbnb/

queue.li_title: Fix & Flip Loans for Beginners: Financing Your First Deal
queue.li_desc: What lenders expect from a first-timer, realistic leverage, the draw process, and the four mistakes that sink first flips.
queue.li:
Nobody funds your fiftieth flip because of your fiftieth flip. They fund it because somebody funded your first one.

First-time flippers do get financed by private lenders. What changes with experience is not access — it is leverage. Experienced borrowers reach up to 92.5% loan-to-cost with us. A first-timer should plan on starting around 85%, which means bringing roughly 15% of total project cost plus reserves. That is not the lender hazing you. Skin in the game on deal one is what keeps a rough first project from becoming a foreclosure instead of a lesson.

What gets underwritten on a first deal:

The numbers — purchase price plus rehab budget against a defensible after-repair value, with total cost landing under roughly 70 to 75% of ARV so there is margin for holding costs and surprises.

Your liquidity — down payment, closing costs, carrying costs for the full timeline, and a contingency of 10 to 15% of the rehab budget. On a $250K project, plan on $50K to $60K accessible.

Your credit — best pricing at 720 and up, solid at 680.

Your team — a licensed GC bid instead of a guess. First-timers who show up with a real scope of work get treated like second-timers.

The rehab money is not handed over at closing. It sits in escrow and releases in draws as work is completed and inspected, which protects you as much as it protects us. Nobody can spend the framing budget before framing exists.

Bridge terms run 6 to 18 months, interest-only, from 9.5%, with closings in as little as 72 hours and a $100K minimum loan size.

queue.li_title: Buying Rental Property in an LLC: How Investor Loans Actually Close
queue.li_desc: Why investors close in an entity, the personal guaranty, the five documents that make an LLC close fast, and the conventional-loan trap.
queue.li:
Every asset-protection attorney says the same thing: hold your rentals in an LLC. Then the investor calls their bank and hears “we can't lend to an LLC.” Both are right, and the gap between them is exactly where investor lending lives.

Conventional Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac mortgages are consumer products. The rules generally require title in your personal name, qualify you on personal debt-to-income, and cap you at ten financed properties. Deeding a conventionally financed house into your LLC after closing works right up until a lender decides to invoke the due-on-sale clause.

DSCR loans are business-purpose loans, so lending to entities is the default rather than the exception. The LLC is the borrower and holds title from day one. The members sign a personal guaranty and credit is pulled on the guarantors — the entity shields you from tenant lawsuits and property liabilities, not from your own loan. Pricing is identical to lending to an individual, because the loan qualifies on the property's rent and the guarantors' credit either way.

What the structure buys you: liability separation, no ten-property cap, portfolio loans that blanket 2 to 10 properties on one note, and an operating agreement that handles partner splits so the loan does not have to.

Five documents make an entity close fast, and having them ready as PDFs before you go under contract is most of the trick: articles of organization, a signed and current operating agreement, the EIN letter, a recent certificate of good standing, and identification for every guarantor.

DSCR rates start at 5.95% on a 30-year fixed, with a $100K minimum loan size.

queue.li_title: Spec Home Construction Loans for Investors: How Ground-Up Financing Works
queue.li_desc: Land plus vertical financing, the two leverage tests, draw schedules, interest on drawn balance, and planning the exit before you break ground.
queue.li:
On an 18-month ground-up build, the term that moves the most money isn't the rate. It's whether interest accrues on the full loan commitment from day one or only on the balance you have actually drawn.

Run the difference. A $600K construction budget where you have drawn $120K for the foundation costs you interest on $120K under drawn-balance terms and interest on $600K under the other kind. Over a year and a half, that gap is a line item large enough to decide whether the spec pencils. Drawn-balance interest is standard on well-structured private construction loans. Read the term sheet for exactly that line before you sign.

The rest of how spec financing is built:

Two leverage tests set your loan. A loan-to-cost ceiling of 85% on land plus vertical, and a completed-value ceiling that typically runs 65 to 70% of the finished appraised value. Your loan is the lesser of the two. A cheap lot with an efficient build clears both comfortably. A premium lot with a luxury build hits the completed-value cap first, which means more cash in. Run both tests before you buy the dirt.

Draws follow milestones. Land funds at closing. The construction budget sits in escrow and releases against foundation, framing and dry-in, mechanicals, drywall and finishes, and final. Photos and invoices in, an app-based inspection confirms percent complete, funds wire in days. Most ground-up builds run 4 to 7 draws.

Plan both exits before you break ground. Sell into a completed-value appraisal that leaves margin after construction interest, points, and commissions, or hold and refinance the finished home into a 30-year DSCR loan and keep it as a brand-new rental. A spec that pencils both ways has no bad outcome.

Our construction box: land plus vertical up to 85% of project cost, from 10%, 18 or 24 month terms, loans from $100K to $7.5M, 42 states. Own the lot free and clear and its equity usually counts toward your contribution.

queue.li_title: DSCR Loan vs. Conventional Mortgage for Rental Property: Which Should Investors Use?
queue.li_desc: Rates, qualification, the 10-property cap, LLC vesting, and speed — compared honestly, including when conventional still wins.
queue.li:
Your first rental got a conventional mortgage. You had a W-2, the bank said yes, the rate was good. Somewhere around rental three or four, that same bank starts saying no.

The difference in one sentence: a conventional investment mortgage qualifies you — your tax returns, your debt-to-income ratio. A DSCR loan qualifies the property — does its rent cover its payment? Everything else follows from that.

Head to head:

Qualification. Conventional wants two years of returns and DTI under roughly 45% counting every property you own. DSCR wants rent divided by PITIA at 1.0 or better, plus your credit score. No income documents.

Rate. Conventional usually wins, though investment-property pricing adjustments narrow the gap. Our DSCR 30-year fixed starts at 5.95% for the highest credit tier at LTV below 60%.

Property cap. Fannie Mae stops at ten financed properties and most banks tap out well before that. DSCR has no cap. This is the wall growing investors actually hit.

Title. Conventional generally wants your personal name on it. DSCR closes in your LLC as standard.

Cash-out seasoning. Conventional says 12 months. We say 3.

Here is the part most lenders skip: conventional is still the right call when you have a strong W-2, you are under the property cap, you are fine holding title personally, and you might sell within a couple of years. First or second rental with clean finances? Take the rate edge.

And a reality check on that edge. Half a point lower on a $250K loan is roughly $80 a month. Against that: no tax-return scramble, title in your entity, no property cap, a 3-month refinance instead of 12, and closing weeks faster on a competitive deal. For someone building a portfolio, $80 a month is the cheapest problem on the list.

Most investors don't choose DSCR because it's cheaper. They choose it because it's the loan that lets them keep buying.

The honest comparison: https://slacapital.ai/blog/dscr-vs-conventional-mortgage/

🏦 Conventional asks what YOU make. DSCR asks what the HOUSE makes.

That one difference explains everything else 👇

📄 Docs — Conventional: 2 yrs tax returns + DTI under ~45%. DSCR: rent ÷ PITIA at 1.0+ and your credit. No income docs.
🔢 Property cap — Conventional: 10 financed properties, max. DSCR: no cap.
🏢 Title — Conventional: your personal name. DSCR: your LLC, standard.
⏱️ Cash-out seasoning — Conventional: 12 months. Us: 3 months.
💵 Rate — Conventional usually wins by a bit. Ours starts at 5.95%, 30-yr fixed.

🤝 And the honest part: if you have a strong W-2, you are under the cap, and you might sell in a couple years — take the conventional rate. We will tell you that.
